aliases: How can I help you today? (Chrome)
features.summary: The message box in every AGI Workforce app. A person types text, adds line breaks, and sees the box grow with the text up to a cap, then scroll. Line breaks are kept in the sent message. Input-method (IME) composition never sends. Web uses a plain textarea by default; a rich editor is behind a switch.

purpose.what_it_does: Lets a person write a message of one or many lines in the composer of Web, Desktop (hosted web app), Mobile, CLI, VS Code and Chrome extension. The box grows as text grows, then scrolls. Enter or a Send control submits; a separate key or control adds a line.
purpose.why_it_exists: Writing a message is the first step of every chat turn. The leaders (ChatGPT, Claude) accept multi-line text, grow the box, and never send mid-composition; the product guidance asks for this explicitly (doc: docs/product/competitive-guidance.md section 5.3, item 17).
purpose.who_uses_it: Every person who chats, on any of the six apps. Developers use the VS Code and CLI composers; browser users use the Chrome side panel.
problems_solved: Long or structured prompts can be typed with line breaks that survive to the model.
An accidental send while choosing an input-method candidate (Chinese, Japanese, Korean) is blocked.
Right-to-left text (Arabic, Hebrew) lines up correctly on the web inputs.
The box does not swallow the screen: it caps its height and scrolls.
use_cases: Type a one-line question and press Enter to send it (web).
Write a three-paragraph prompt using Shift+Enter between paragraphs, then send.
On a phone, type a long message; Return adds lines and the arrow button sends.
In a terminal, press Alt+Enter or Shift+Enter (or Ctrl+J where Shift+Enter never arrives) to add a line.

established.statement: The user can type a plain-text message and send it (S13.01); multi-line text keeps its line breaks (S13.02).
The composer grows taller automatically up to a cap, then scrolls (S13.03). A key such as Shift+Enter inserts a newline without sending (S13.09).
Handle multiline input, growing height, composition events and non-Latin keyboards without accidental sends.
Mobile text input is multi-line capable, keyboard-safe, sends on explicit action, and must not resize or overlap badly on small devices.

features.summary: A visible round button sends the message. While a reply is running the same slot turns into Stop on web, mobile and Chrome; VS Code shows a separate Stop button beside a Queue or Steer send; the CLI uses Esc or Ctrl-C. Send is disabled when blocked. The web holds a message that looks like it contains a key or password once.

purpose.what_it_does: Submits the composed message and ends a running reply on demand. The control shows Send, a busy spinner, or Stop according to the turn state, and is disabled when sending is blocked.
purpose.why_it_exists: A person needs a clear way to send and a clear way to stop a long or wrong reply. The requirements ask for send and stop controls on every composer (doc: docs/product/requirements.md section 6.1, section 10.7: Send when idle, stop while running).
purpose.who_uses_it: Every person on all six apps.
problems_solved: Stopping a long reply saves cost and time.
Sending an unsupported mix (attachment and tool) is prevented instead of failing later.
Pasting a credential into a chat by mistake is caught once on web.
use_cases: Click the arrow to send; click the square to stop a reply that is going the wrong way.
Press Escape in the web composer to stop when no menu is open.
See the send arrow greyed out while offline.
Send a message that contains an API key: the web holds it with a warning; send again to continue.

Chrome: signed-in managed cloud chat ready (side_panel.ts:9945).

3. While the reply streams the slot shows Stop.

CLI Stop breaks out of the running request, keeps the partial answer, reconciles session history, records 'generation_stopped'.

features.summary: Choose whether Enter sends or adds a line, and use undo and redo while writing. Web has a 'Send with Enter' switch (the rich editor ignores it), VS Code has a 'Send key' setting, mobile, CLI and Chrome have no setting. Undo is browser-native on web, has its own stack in the CLI, and is unverified on mobile and VS Code.

purpose.why_it_exists: People who write long prompts or use input methods want Enter to add a line. The guidance lists 'Enter preferences' (doc: docs/product/competitive-guidance.md section 5.3, item 17).

purpose.why_it_exists: The automatic box caps its height (240px on web). Long prompts need a bigger area. The brief asks for manual enlargement and full-screen or external editing.

features.summary: What happens when a person pastes. Files and images become attachments. Text of 10,000 characters or more becomes a file 'Pasted text.txt' (web) or a chip (mobile). Code is wrapped in a fence with an undo link (web). The CLI collapses long pastes to a placeholder. VS Code and Chrome handle files only.

purpose.what_it_does: Decides what a paste turns into: plain text in the box, attachments, a long-text file, or a fenced code block.
purpose.why_it_exists: Huge pastes would flood the box and break the length cap; code needs a block; files should attach. The guidance lists drag, drop and paste with per-file validation and long prompts without accidental sends (doc: docs/product/competitive-guidance.md section 5.3, items 17 and 18).
purpose.who_uses_it: Everyone who pastes text, screenshots or code.
problems_solved: A book-sized paste floods or freezes the box.
Pasted code loses its layout in markdown.
A copied image does not have to be saved as a file first.
use_cases: Paste a screenshot to attach it.
Paste 50,000 characters of a log; it becomes 'Pasted text.txt'.
Paste a function; it is fenced with triple backticks and 'Paste as plain text' undoes it.
In the CLI paste a long block; it shows [Pasted text #1 +N lines] and expands on send.

features.summary: The public /pricing page on web (and in the Desktop window, which loads the hosted web app) shows every plan side by side with localized prices, a comparison table, and a Monthly/Annual switch for Team. Mobile shows a read-only plan screen. VS Code has a Compare Plans pick list. None of these sell on mobile, VS Code, CLI or Chrome.

purpose.what_it_does: Shows what each AGI Workforce plan costs and includes before a person chooses. On web it also lets the buyer pick monthly or yearly billing for Team and starts the buy flow from the plan button.
purpose.why_it_exists: A buyer must see price, usage and features side by side and see tax and billing terms before paying (brief S83.01, S83.02). Prices must come from the shared plan catalog and from localized Stripe prices, not from numbers typed into screens (AGENTS.md section 4).
purpose.who_uses_it: Visitors, Free users deciding to upgrade, paying users looking at a higher plan, and team buyers choosing seats and cadence.
problems_solved: Buyer cannot judge plans without a side-by-side view.
Buyer in India sees prices that include GST while others see prices without tax; the page says which.
A region without a configured price must not offer a button that fails later.
Team buyers need a yearly option only where a yearly price is really configured.
use_cases: A visitor opens /pricing, switches to the Business tab and compares Team seat prices monthly versus annual.
A Free user clicks a paid plan button and is sent to sign in, then returns to /pricing.
A Premium subscriber opens /upgrade from chat and sees the next plan up with what it adds.
A VS Code user runs Code: Compare Plans to see what each plan adds and opens the web page.

A monthly/annual toggle changes displayed prices and the cadence charged.

steps.what_happens: Browser loads /pricing and asks GET /api/pricing/localized for prices.
Server looks up each configured price, expands currency options and marks it checkoutReady only when amount and tax behaviour match.
Page computes the cadence: Annual is offered only if the yearly Team price is ready; the default is Annual for buyers without a paid plan, else the cadence of the live subscription.
Page reads the buyer's plan and upgrade-access state to decide the button text and whether it is enabled.
On mobile, the plans screen reads the plan from the tier store and renders catalog text; no purchase call is made in the shipped build.

purpose.who_uses_it: Free users and returning customers with no live paid plan on web and Desktop; staff who open or close the paid-upgrade gate.
problems_solved: Double billing across Stripe, Apple, Google and organization grants.
Paying but not seeing the plan active.

Two open checkout pages racing to create two subscriptions.

features.summary: A paying web user moves to a higher plan mid-cycle. The app asks the server for a priced preview (credit for unused time, subtotal, discount, tax, total due today), lets the person add a promotion code, and on confirm charges the saved card with a signed preview token. A new billing period starts that day.

purpose.what_it_does: Previews and applies an upgrade of a live Stripe subscription, with proration lines, tax, an optional promotion code, and a confirmation.
purpose.why_it_exists: Upgrades must explain proration: credit for unused time, the charge today, and when renewal happens (S83.05), and users can enter a promotion code when buying (S83.07). Charging a saved card needs explicit assent.
purpose.who_uses_it: Paying web and Desktop users on Basic, Premium or Max moving up, and Team owners adding seats or moving from an individual plan to Team.
problems_solved: Surprise charges: the dialog shows what will be taken today.
Stale prices: the token expires after 10 minutes and must match user, plan, interval, seats and code.
Silent coupon failure: a bad code shows an error and nothing changes.
Free-to-paid users with no card to credit are sent to full checkout rather than a fake proration.

established.statement: Upgrades explain proration: credit for unused time, the charge today and when the next renewal happens.
Users can enter a coupon or promotion code when buying.
An immediate tier upgrade starts a new billing period that day and charges the new price minus credit for unused time; if payment is incomplete or fails the old plan stays.
Preview and charge share one signed proration timestamp; a seat increase keeps the renewal date.
Usage never resets on upgrade; consumed usage and purchased balance carry forward.

acceptance_criteria: The preview lists real proration lines and a Total due today equal to what Stripe takes.
A stale or mismatched preview token makes confirm fail and tells the user to preview again.
A valid promotion code shows a discount row and its description; an invalid code shows an error and leaves the total unchanged.
If the card needs extra action, the old plan stays active and a payment link is offered.
A user whose plan has no paid charge to credit sees the non-prorated explanation and a start-checkout button.
After confirm the plan changes only after the webhook; the screen does not claim activation before it can be read.
A store-billed or organization-managed user cannot start this flow.

steps.what_happens: Settings, Billing loads and calls GET /api/billing/payment-methods and invoices together.
Server finds the customer and asks the provider for the customer, subscription default and payment methods.
User clicks a manage button; page posts /api/portal with CSRF and an idempotency key.
Server checks owner policy and gate, then creates the portal session with a safe return path.
Browser goes to the portal (Desktop opens the system browser); the user edits cards there.
On return the window rereads the plan and billing queries.
